# Collections and items

Collections (their key, label and fields) and their items, one at a time or imported in one step. Read `data` first: it lists the collections with their ids, fields and items.

[`collection.create`](#collectioncreate) · [`collection.set`](#collectionset) · [`collection.remove`](#collectionremove) · [`collection.restore`](#collectionrestore) · [`collection.setField`](#collectionsetfield) · [`collection.removeField`](#collectionremovefield) · [`item.create`](#itemcreate) · [`item.set`](#itemset) · [`item.remove`](#itemremove) · [`item.restore`](#itemrestore) · [`item.import`](#itemimport) · [`item.revert`](#itemrevert)

## collection.create

Add a collection to the site: its key (what repeats and dynamic pages name), its label and its fields, with no items yet. Add or change fields later with collection.setField and items with item.create or item.import. Refused: `collection.exists` (the id or the key is taken), `collection.field` (a field key listed twice, or a reference field naming a collection the site does not have).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | A new uuid you choose for the collection: the id later ops name it by. |
| `key` | string (max 60) | yes | The collection's key, what repeats and dynamic pages name: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, - or _. |
| `label` | string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, string (min 1, max 120)> |  | What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }). |
| `fields` | ({ key: string (max 60), type: string (max 40), localized: boolean, label?: string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, string (min 1, max 120)>, required?: boolean, collection?: string (max 60), multiple?: boolean, options?: ({ value: string (max 40), label: string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, …> })[] (≤100), fields… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) |  |  |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","key":"progetti","label":{"it":"Progetti","en":"Projects"},"fields":[{"key":"title","type":"text","localized":true,"label":{"it":"Titolo","en":"Title"},"required":true},{"key":"year","type":"number","localized":false,"label":{"it":"Anno","en":"Year"}},{"key":"cover","type":"media","localized":false,"label":{"it":"Copertina","en":"Cover"}},{"key":"kind","type":"select","localized":false,"label":{"it":"Tipo","en":"Kind"},"options":[{"value":"restauro","label":{"it":"Restauro","en":"Restoration"}},{"value":"residenziale","label":{"it":"Residenziale","en":"Residential"}}]}]}
```

## collection.set

Rename a collection (its label or its key), or name the field that titles each item and the one its address is made from. titleField and slugField name a field of the collection; null takes the choice off. Fields left out stay as they are. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.exists` (another collection has the key), `collection.inUse` (a new key while a repeat, a dynamic page or another collection's reference field reads the old one; detail.readers names them), `collection.field` (titleField or slugField names no field of it).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `key` | string (max 60) |  | The collection's key, what repeats and dynamic pages name: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, - or _. |
| `label` | string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, string (min 1, max 120)> \| null |  | Its new label; null takes the label off (the key reads as its name). |
| `titleField` | string (max 60) \| null |  | A field of the collection, by key; null takes the choice off (the first text field titles the item). |
| `slugField` | string (max 60) \| null |  | A field of the collection, by key; null takes the choice off (the first text field titles the item). |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","label":{"it":"Lavori","en":"Works"},"titleField":"title","slugField":"title"}
```

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48"}
```

## collection.restore

Put a collection's definition back whole as it was, its items untouched. Libretto writes it as the undo of collection.remove, collection.set and the field ops; a batch that sends it is refused (only Libretto makes it). On an undo it is refused with `collection.exists` when another collection took its key since.

- **op**; class `reserved` (no one sends it: Libretto writes it); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `definition` | Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>>> | yes | The collection definition whole: { key, label, fields, titleField, slugField }. |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","definition":{"key":"progetti","label":{"it":"Progetti","en":"Projects"},"fields":[{"key":"title","type":"text","localized":true,"label":{"it":"Titolo","en":"Title"}}]}}
```

## collection.setField

Add one field to a collection, or change one: its type, whether it holds one value per language, its label, whether an item must give it, a list's columns or its place among the fields. A field with a key the collection has is changed, else added. A reference names its target collection (by key) and multiple, a select its options, a list its columns (fields). What the field stores beside what the op says (its help; its label, required and columns when not said) and the other fields stay as they are. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.field` (over 200 fields, or a reference to a collection the site does not have), `item.value` (a reference or select changed so a value an item holds no longer fits: change those items with item.set first).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `field` | object | yes |  |
| `field` › `key` | string (max 60) | yes | A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _. |
| `field` › `type` | string (max 40) | yes | What the field holds: text, richtext, number, boolean, date, colour, media, link, list, json, reference, select, mediaList, file. A reference names its target collection, a select its options, a list its columns. |
| `field` › `localized` | boolean | yes | true: an item holds one value per language ({ "it": …, "en": … }); false: one value for every language. |
| `field` › `label` | string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, string (min 1, max 120)> |  | What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }). |
| `field` › `required` | boolean |  | Whether an item gives it a value before it goes live (the admin asks for it). Absent: as stored. |
| `field` › `collection` | string (max 60) |  | A reference field's target collection, by key. |
| `field` › `multiple` | boolean |  | A reference field: true holds a list of item uids (at most 200), false or absent one. |
| `field` › `options` | ({ value: string (max 40), label: string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, string (min 1, max 120)> })[] (≤100) |  |  |
| `field` › `fields` | ({ key: string (max 60), type: string (max 40), label?: string (min 1, max 120) \| Record<string, string (min 1, max 120)>, localized?: boolean })[] (≤30) |  |  |
| `index` | integer ≥0 |  | Its place among the fields, from 0; absent: where it is, or last for a new field. |
| `rewriteAll` | true |  | Leave it out: it marks entries an older version of the op stored, which rewrote every field. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","field":{"key":"place","type":"text","localized":false,"label":{"it":"Luogo","en":"Place"}},"index":2}
```
```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","field":{"key":"architects","type":"reference","localized":false,"label":{"it":"Architetti","en":"Architects"},"collection":"persone","multiple":true}}
```

## collection.removeField

Remove one field from a collection; items keep the values they hold for it, unread, so putting the field back shows them again. The other fields stay as they are; a template that shows the field shows nothing there. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.field` (no such field), `collection.inUse` (a repeat filters, sorts or picks by it; detail.readers names them).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `key` | string (max 60) | yes | A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _. |
| `rewriteAll` | true |  | Leave it out: it marks entries an older version of the op stored, which rewrote every field. |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","key":"place"}
```

A value for a field the collection does not have is kept, unread. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.exists` (the id is taken), `item.slug` (another item has the slug), `item.value` (a value that does not fit its field: its type, a select's options, a reference's target items).

| `collection` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `id` | uuid | yes | A new uuid you choose for the item: its uid. |
| `slug` | string (max 200) \| Record<string, string (max 200)> | yes | The item's address under its collection's page: lowercase letters, digits and -, unique in the collection; or one per language ({ "it": "casa-sul-lago", "en": "lake-house" }). |
| `status` | string (max 40) |  | draft (kept off the live site) or published (live with the next publish). |
| `position` | number |  | Its place among the items: lower comes first. |
| `values` | Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>>> |  | Values by field key. A per-language field takes one value per locale ({ "en": …, "it": … }). A richtext field takes a text (read as paragraphs split on blank lines) or prose blocks { children, nodes }: children lists the top-level node ids in order, nodes maps each id (8 lowercase letters or digits) to its node. Blocks: a paragraph or heading { kind: "text", as: "p" \| "h2"…"h6", runs } and a code block (as "pre"); a quote { kind: "frame", as: "blockquote", children: [paragraphs] }; a list { kind: "frame", as: "ul" \| "ol", start?, children: [{ kind: "text", as: "li", runs } or { kind: "frame", as: "li", children: [paragraphs, lists] }] }; a figure { kind: "frame", as: "figure", children: [{ kind: "image", src: { $media }, alt }, then optionally { kind: "frame", as: "figcaption", children: [paragraphs] }] }. ## item.import

Add many items to a collection in one step, all of them or none (a file's rows, at most 500). Each row: a new id, its slug, status (draft unless said) and values by field; the rows go after the items there, in order. Each row is checked as item.create checks one, and a value for a field the collection does not have is refused (`item.field`). Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.exists`, `item.slug` (a slug taken, by an item or an earlier row), `item.value`, `item.field`; each refusal names its row (detail.row, from 1).

- **op**; class `content` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "event", "entry", "csv", "spreadsheet", "import".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collection` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `items` | ({ id: uuid, slug: string (max 200) \| Record<string, string (max 200)>, status?: string (max 40), values?: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>> })[] (≤500) | yes | The rows, in the order they go after the items there. |

Example input:

```json
{"collection":"c41f7a2e-9b3d-4e61-8a05-2f6d9c1e7b48","items":[{"id":"5d2e8f14-7a3b-4c96-b1e0-9f4a6c2d8e73","slug":"casa-sul-lago","values":{"title":{"it":"Casa sul lago","en":"Lake house"},"year":2023,"kind":"residenziale"}},{"id":"8a3c1e5f-2b7d-4f09-9c64-1e8b3d5a7f20","slug":"palazzo-santa-croce","status":"published","values":{"title":{"it":"Palazzo Santa Croce","en":"Palazzo Santa Croce"},"year":2021,"kind":"restauro"}}]}
```

## item.revert

Bring one item back as an earlier step left it: its record (slug, status, values) whole, in one step. Its place among the items stays as the draft has it. Use it for an item that is still in the draft; a removed item comes back through the undo of its removal. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.unknown` (the item is not in the draft), `item.revertMissing` (detail: missing field or item, and their names) when the record holds a value for a field the collection no longer has, or a reference names an item that is gone.

- **op**; class `content` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "bring", "recover".

|---|---|---|---|
| `collection` | uuid | yes | The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key). |
| `id` | uuid | yes | The item, by its uid (the data read lists each item with it). |
